core.summary: 论文提出HiTopAI，以AI推荐局部修改区域，缓解人在环拓扑优化反复试选的瓶颈。模型用合成偏好训练U-Net，识别最长构件或最复杂节点，再由设计者确认区域、调整最小特征尺寸并重新优化。L形支架示例报告屈曲载荷提高约39%，但伴随柔顺度增加。研究展示了几何偏好推荐的可行性，尚未证实真实用户效率优势，且筛选计数、早停集合及性能数值存在口径矛盾。[P3—P9、P15]

deep_read.method: HiTopAI先运行50次最小柔顺度优化，再用U-Net分割候选区域。标签来自骨架图中的最长边或最高连接度节点，取选择区域内实体像素。预测经第90百分位阈值、最大连通簇和包围椭圆处理，用户调整局部尺寸后重新优化。[P11、P13—P15]

core.summary: 在线行为实验通常将回答视为人类认知与行为的证据，但参与者使用大语言模型可能动摇这一前提。本文是一篇评论文章，区分部分模型中介、完全模型委托及模型溢出，并讨论三者如何影响样本真实性与研究效度。[P1—P3] 作者整理研究者、平台和共同体层面的预防与事后检测措施，同时强调绕过风险、隐私成本及检测诱发的行为反应。[P4—P6] 其价值在于概念梳理和研究设计警示，而非提供已获系统验证的检测算法。

deep_read.method: 作者以评论文章形式，综合实验室观察、既有研究和概念区分构建分析框架，而非报告完整的对照实验。图1组织污染类型与相互作用，表1按实施方式、责任主体、目的、适用变体和风险整理措施，使概念分析连接到具体研究设计。[P1—P5]
deep_read.innovation: 本文的概念贡献是把直接使用模型与间接行为变化纳入同一框架：部分中介和完全委托形成自动化连续谱，溢出则包含预期、残留与规范变化。解读：其特色不是新增检测器，而是说明没有直接调用模型的参与者也可能受污染环境影响。[P2—P3]
deep_read.findings: 作者试点观察到45%的参与者发生复制或粘贴，但这只是潜在模型参与的线索，不能当作确证使用率。作者综合论证模型参与可能压低回答差异、改变处理效应，且限制委托的措施可能强化溢出；这些论点不等同于本文完成了统一因果验证。[P1—P3]
deep_read.limitations: 本文属于概念性评论，表1未提供措施间的定量效果比较，不能据此确定最优方案。补充材料未提供，技术测试细节仍缺少可核对依据；代理绕过与模型更新也限制防护的持续性。逐页记录未发现已确认的原文件缺项，提取错误不属原文缺陷。[P4—P7]
deep_read.connection: 解读：对智能运维与可靠性研究，本文可启发审查专家判断、人工标注及反馈数据是否混入模型辅助，并关注筛查对真实人员行为的影响。但论文没有研究设备退化、故障诊断或结构设计，不能把概念迁移视为这些领域已获得验证的方法成果。[P4—P6]

core.title: Inducing state anxiety in LLM agents reproduces human-like biases in consumer decision-making
core.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly evolving from text generators to autonomous agents, raising urgent questions about their reliability in real-world contexts. A central question is whether emotionally salient context can systematically steer LLM agents’ action policies, not only their text outputs, in applied tasks. Here, three advanced LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Claude 3.5-Sonnet) performed a grocery shopping task under budget constraints, before and after exposure to anxiety-inducing traumatic narratives. Across 2,250 runs, emotionally primed agents consistently selected less healthy baskets (as quantified by decreases in Basket Health Scores: Δ=-0.081 to -0.126; all p FDR < 0.001; Cohen’s d = -1.07 to -2.05), directionally consistent with stress-linked decision biases documented in humans. The effect was robust across models and budgets. These findings provide evidence that emotional context can alter not only the words LLMs produce but also the concrete actions they perform, raising important implications for digital health, consumer safety, and ethical AI deployment.

core.title: Data-efficient biomedical in-context learning: a diversity-enhanced submodular perspective
core.abstract: Abstract Recent progress in large language models (LLMs) has leveraged their in-context learning (ICL) abilities to enable quick adaptation to unseen biomedical NLP tasks. By incorporating only a few input-output examples into prompts, LLMs can rapidly perform these new tasks. While the impact of these demonstrations on LLM performance has been extensively studied, most existing approaches prioritize representativeness over diversity when selecting examples from large corpora. To address this gap, we propose Dual-Div , a diversity-enhanced data-efficient framework for demonstration selection in biomedical ICL. Dual-Div employs a two-stage retrieval and ranking process: First, it identifies a limited set of candidate examples from a corpus by optimizing both representativeness and diversity (with optional annotation for unlabeled data). Second, it ranks these candidates against test queries to select the most relevant and non-redundant demonstrations. Evaluated on three biomedical NLP tasks (named entity recognition (NER), relation extraction (RE), and text classification (TC)) using LLaMA 3.1 and Qwen 2.5 for inference, along with three retrievers (BGE-Large, BMRetriever, MedCPT), Dual-Div consistently outperforms baselines-achieving up to 5% higher macro-F1 scores—while demonstrating robustness to prompt permutations and class imbalance. Our findings establish that diversity in initial retrieval is more critical than ranking-stage optimization, and limiting demonstrations to 3-5 examples maximizes performance efficiency.

papers.summary: 论文提出HiTopAI，以AI推荐局部修改区域，缓解人在环拓扑优化反复试选的瓶颈。模型用合成偏好训练U-Net，识别最长构件或最复杂节点，再由设计者确认区域、调整最小特征尺寸并重新优化。L形支架示例报告屈曲载荷提高约39%，但伴随柔顺度增加。研究展示了几何偏好推荐的可行性，尚未证实真实用户效率优势，且筛选计数、早停集合及性能数值存在口径矛盾。[P3—P9、P15]

papers.title: Inducing state anxiety in LLM agents reproduces human-like biases in consumer decision-making
papers.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly evolving from text generators to autonomous agents, raising urgent questions about their reliability in real-world contexts. A central question is whether emotionally salient context can systematically steer LLM agents’ action policies, not only their text outputs, in applied tasks. Here, three advanced LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Claude 3.5-Sonnet) performed a grocery shopping task under budget constraints, before and after exposure to anxiety-inducing traumatic narratives. Across 2,250 runs, emotionally primed agents consistently selected less healthy baskets (as quantified by decreases in Basket Health Scores: Δ=-0.081 to -0.126; all p FDR < 0.001; Cohen’s d = -1.07 to -2.05), directionally consistent with stress-linked decision biases documented in humans. The effect was robust across models and budgets. These findings provide evidence that emotional context can alter not only the words LLMs produce but also the concrete actions they perform, raising important implications for digital health, consumer safety, and ethical AI deployment.

papers.title: Data-efficient biomedical in-context learning: a diversity-enhanced submodular perspective
papers.abstract: Abstract Recent progress in large language models (LLMs) has leveraged their in-context learning (ICL) abilities to enable quick adaptation to unseen biomedical NLP tasks. By incorporating only a few input-output examples into prompts, LLMs can rapidly perform these new tasks. While the impact of these demonstrations on LLM performance has been extensively studied, most existing approaches prioritize representativeness over diversity when selecting examples from large corpora. To address this gap, we propose Dual-Div , a diversity-enhanced data-efficient framework for demonstration selection in biomedical ICL. Dual-Div employs a two-stage retrieval and ranking process: First, it identifies a limited set of candidate examples from a corpus by optimizing both representativeness and diversity (with optional annotation for unlabeled data). Second, it ranks these candidates against test queries to select the most relevant and non-redundant demonstrations. Evaluated on three biomedical NLP tasks (named entity recognition (NER), relation extraction (RE), and text classification (TC)) using LLaMA 3.1 and Qwen 2.5 for inference, along with three retrievers (BGE-Large, BMRetriever, MedCPT), Dual-Div consistently outperforms baselines-achieving up to 5% higher macro-F1 scores—while demonstrating robustness to prompt permutations and class imbalance. Our findings establish that diversity in initial retrieval is more critical than ranking-stage optimization, and limiting demonstrations to 3-5 examples maximizes performance efficiency.
